limits: Multiple design variables changed; this is not a controlled causal comparison.
Current costs include endpoint approaches but remain Manhattan/node-center estimates. Earlier artifacts use a different timing basis; do not compare their costs or call them measured travel time.

observations: An independent middle bridge crosses the lower Workshop-Separator trench; compiled hull samples and solid-separator traces pass.
The two upper armor rooms have separate middle and upper connections, while strong weapons and recovery remain below.
The incident route count is less concentrated than Switchback, but real route use has not been observed.
The median sampled world sightline is longer and p90 shorter than Switchback; these describe a different distribution rather than a quality score.
Major-item separation exceeds the small-DM descriptive band; this needs an empty-travel and capacity playtest.
reusable_improvements: Point-aware placement costs include same-node XY distance and cross-node approaches, with explicit flow cost-basis metadata.
Point lights can occupy valid sealed passage volumes without relaxing gameplay room binding.
Recipe export and the new viewer use explicit stair runs and declared floor levels.
One build/inspection pipeline supports both recipes, optional earlier-map comparison and compiled overpass/hull checks.
controlled_variants_pending: Close only the eastern Outfall-Control bypass.
Close only the upper Separator-Control return.
Move only one upper armor to a validated middle socket.
Move only Mega Health closer to Intake.
runtime_questions: Do four and six players use distinct circuits, or does the larger area cause empty travel?
Can lower players recover while an opponent controls the upper armor circuit?
Are the low trench, gallery undersides and exits readable in the target renderer?
Does the overpass improve route choice and recognition without causing unwanted pursuit breaks?
